step1_analysis.circuit_type: Baseband Programmable Gain Amplifier (PGA) / Active Filter Cell
step1_analysis.description: A fully differential pseudo-differential telescopic cascode amplifier with a cross-coupled NMOS active load (negative gm cell) to boost gain or provide filtering. The netlist contains a likely extraction typo (node N1 instead of N5) which breaks the symmetry of the cross-coupled pair.

paper_reference.title: A Single-Chip Multimode Receiver for GSM900, DCS1800, PCS1900, and WCDMA

voltage_gain.description: Differential AC voltage gain at low frequencies.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain is determined by the transconductance of the PMOS input pair (XM3, XM4) and the high output impedance of the cascode, boosted by the negative gm of the cross-coupled pair (XM5, XM6). Assuming gm ~ 300uS and Rout ~ 100kOhm, Gain = gm * Rout ~ 30 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cross-coupled pair significantly boosts the DC gain, making it highly dependent on the exact matching of positive and negative conductances.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the amplifier block.

sky130_expected.calculation: 4 PMOS branches at ~37.5 uA each + 4 NMOS branches at ~19.4 uA each. Total current ~ 220 uA. Power = 1.8V * 220uA = 0.396 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on the provided bias voltages (VB1=0.54V, VB3=0.99V) and SKY130 device parameters.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency at which the differential voltage gain drops to 0 dB.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_ug = gm / (2 * pi * CL). With gm = 300 uS and CL = 1 pF, f_ug ~ 47 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the load capacitance applied in the testbench.

out_of_band_iip2.description: Second-order input intercept point for out-of-band interferers.

sky130_expected.calculation: Requires highly symmetric layout and perfectly matched differential pairs. In schematic simulation, IIP2 is artificially high (often >100 dBm) due to perfect mathematical symmetry.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Reported as a key metric in the paper for the baseband circuitry.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, unity gain frequency, and transient output swing. A zero-volt source is used to fix a likely netlist extraction typo (N1 -> N5) to restore the symmetry of the cross-coupled pair. Ideal CMFB is added to stabilize the high-impedance nodes.
